<description>
Currently we have no automation in place to check that our code signing certificates are not expired or close to expiry. We have previously "relied on Release Candidates" as a dry-run for codesigners to realise that a certificate has expired and have time to fix it. "Noticing during RC cycle" also might not be appropriate in the future if we release more bugfix minor/patch releases on short notice.

In place of this process we can run a weekly CI job which will check the certificate's validity and open an issue when it passes an expiry threshold.

In this draft we only check the windows cert (as I couldn't find a mac one) and we set the alert threshold to 90 days.

When the threshold is passed, the job will open an issue in this repo (optionally tagging relevant key-holders).
</description>

<commits>
aceb05c436 ci: Monitor Windows signing certificate expiry and

...revocation.

Check the signing certificate on master weekly so maintainers have time
to renew it before Windows release signing is affected. Open an issue
within 90 days of expiry, including certificate details and the checked
commit.

A signing certificate can also be revoked (before its expiry warning
window). Fetch and validate its CRL so the weekly monitor can report
confirmed revocation without treating network or verification failures
as certificate replacement alerts.
</commits>

diff --git a/.github/workflows/code-signing-certificate.yml b/.github/workflows/code-signing-certificate.yml
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..032e7644a8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/code-signing-certificate.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,73 @@
+# Copyright (c) 2026-present The Bitcoin Core developers
+# Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying
+# file COPYING or https://opensource.org/license/mit.
+
+name: Code signing certificate
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+  schedule:
+    # Mondays at 09:23 UTC.
+    - cron: '23 9 * * 1'
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  issues: write
+
+concurrency:
+  group: code-signing-certificate
+
+jobs:
+  check-certificate:
+    if: github.repository == 'bitcoin/bitcoin'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-slim
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          ref: master
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Check certificate
+        id: certificate
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          status=0
+          ./contrib/devtools/check-code-signing-certificates.py > "$RUNNER_TEMP/certificate-report.txt" || status=$?
+          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/certificate-report.txt"
+          if (( status == 3 )); then
+            echo "warning=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          else
+            exit "$status"
+          fi
+
+      - name: Report certificate warning
+        if: steps.certificate.outputs.warning == 'true'
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          GH_REPO: bitcoin/bitcoin
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          export TITLE="Code signing certificate warning"
+          REPORT=$(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/certificate-report.txt")
+          export REPORT
+          # Include closed issues so closing an alert acknowledges this report.
+          EXISTING=$(gh issue list --state all --search "\"$TITLE\" in:title" \
+            --json title,body,url --jq '.[] | select(.title == env.TITLE) | select(.body | contains(env.REPORT)) | .url')
+          if [[ -n "$EXISTING" ]]; then
+            echo "Certificate warning already reported: $EXISTING"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+
+          COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
+          cat > "$RUNNER_TEMP/certificate-issue.md" <<EOF
+          Code signing certificates need replacement. Please update the certificates listed below and backport the updates to maintained release branches.
+
+          Certificates checked on [master at $COMMIT]($GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GH_REPO/tree/$COMMIT):
+
+          \`\`\`text
+          $REPORT
+          \`\`\`
+
+          [Weekly check]($GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GH_REPO/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID).
+          EOF
+          gh issue create --title "$TITLE" --body-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/certificate-issue.md"
diff --git a/contrib/devtools/check-code-signing-certificates.py b/contrib/devtools/check-code-signing-certificates.py
new file mode 100755
index 0000000000..9c8d28ced2
--- /dev/null
+++ b/contrib/devtools/check-code-signing-certificates.py
@@ -0,0 +1,120 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# Copyright (c) 2026-present The Bitcoin Core developers
+# Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying
+# file COPYING or https://opensource.org/license/mit.
+
+import http.client
+import re
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import urllib.request
+
+
+# Format: /path/to/cert, <expiry in days>
+CERTIFICATES = [
+    ("contrib/windeploy/win-codesign.cert", 90),
+]
+# Exit 0 if checks pass, 2 if any check fails, and 3 if any certificate needs
+# replacement. Reserve 1 for unhandled Python errors.
+
+
+def output(*command: str) -> str:
+    return subprocess.check_output(command, text=True).rstrip("\n")
+
+
+def check_certificate(cert: str, days: int) -> tuple[str, bool]:
+    x509 = ["openssl", "x509", "-in", cert, "-noout"]
+    extensions = output(*x509, "-ext", "basicConstraints,extendedKeyUsage")
+    # Require the first certificate to be a non-CA code signing certificate.
+    if "CA:FALSE" not in extensions or "Code Signing" not in extensions:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"The first certificate in {cert} must be a non-CA code signing certificate."
+        )
+
+    expiry = output(*x509, "-enddate").removeprefix("notAfter=")
+    warning_check = subprocess.run(
+        [*x509, "-checkend", str(days * 86400)], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL
+    )
+    if warning_check.returncode == 0:
+        distribution_points = output(*x509, "-ext", "crlDistributionPoints")
+        crl_url = re.search(r"URI:(https?://\S+)", distribution_points)
+        if crl_url is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"No HTTP CRL distribution point found in {cert}.")
+        # Download separately to avoid older OpenSSL versions' 100 KiB limit.
+        with (
+            urllib.request.urlopen(crl_url[1], timeout=30) as response,
+            tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile() as crl,
+        ):
+            shutil.copyfileobj(response, crl)
+            crl.flush()
+            verification = subprocess.run(
+                [
+                    "openssl",
+                    "verify",
+                    "-crl_check",
+                    "-CRLfile",
+                    crl.name,
+                    "-untrusted",
+                    cert,
+                    cert,
+                ],
+                capture_output=True,
+                text=True,
+                timeout=30,
+            )
+        if verification.returncode == 0:
+            return (
+                f"{cert}: CRL check passed; expires {expiry} (at least {days} days away).",
+                False,
+            )
+        # Only alert on leaf revocation with no other verification errors,
+        # such as a stale CRL that also contains the certificate's serial.
+        errors = re.findall(
+            r"^error (\d+) at (\d+) depth lookup:", verification.stderr, re.MULTILINE
+        )
+        if errors != [("23", "0")]:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Revocation check failed for {cert}:\n{verification.stderr}"
+            )
+        reason = "has been revoked"
+    else:
+        # Preserve renewal alerts even when the CRL service is unavailable.
+        reason = "is expiring or has expired"
+
+    details = output(*x509, "-subject", "-issuer", "-dates", "-sha256", "-fingerprint")
+    # Keep the report stable when an expiring certificate becomes expired,
+    # so CI can recognize an already acknowledged alert.
+    return (
+        f"{cert}: {reason}.\nWarning window: {days} days.\n{details}",
+        True,
+    )
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    reports = []
+    warnings = []
+    failed = False
+    for cert, days in CERTIFICATES:
+        try:
+            report, warning = check_certificate(cert, days)
+            reports.append(report)
+            if warning:
+                warnings.append(report)
+        except (
+            http.client.HTTPException,
+            OSError,
+            subprocess.SubprocessError,
+            ValueError,
+        ) as error:
+            print(error, file=sys.stderr)
+            failed = True
+    print("\n\n".join(warnings or reports))
+    if failed:
+        return 2
+    return 3 if warnings else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
